endorsements.quote: Once model training is complete, and the model performs well on the originally selected test set, external validation is crucial to reduce the risk of inherent biases before it is deployed and, later, fine‐tuned for further performance improvements.
This phase involves ongoing monitoring and reviewing of the model to adapt to changing data and ensure consistent performance [ 10 ].
Stakeholder involvement Clinical and technical stakeholders are engaged from the beginning with a clear plan
Algorithmic accountability Responsibility chain for AI decisions clearly documented
Ethical evaluation Project reviewed by ethics committee; ethical evaluation following the European Federation of National Associations of Orthopaedics and Traumatology (EFORT) guidelines
Outcome measures Patient‐centered and clinical outcome metrics are clearly defined
Impact on clinical workflow Project is designed to integrate into or inform clinical workflows

Secondary effects on the clinical setting where the model and solution is being used, as well as secondary effects on patients, will have to be continuously considered and actions taken to mitigate any negative effects.

unlisted_practices: Train AI models on data that closely resemble the format and quality of data expected during use.
Orthopaedic researchers should team up with statistics and AI experts when selecting AI technology.
Perform a broad financial and medical effects analysis of AI introduction over short, medium and long term.
Consider cost-effective and scalable AI alternatives to improve accessibility for a wider variety of institutions.
Use reporting checklists such as TRIPOD-AI, TRIPOD-LLM or PROBAST-AI when developing and validating models.
Use explainability tools such as SHAP/LIME to enhance model interpretability.
Use common data standards such as FHIR to improve data aggregation.
Plan project budget and time for data cleaning, labeling, model refinement and post-deployment monitoring.

screen.reason: This is a practical guide/guideline framework offering recommendations (resource management checklist) for AI implementation in orthopaedic research and practice.
